comparisons.peer_summary: On November 22, 2023, Broadcom acquired VMware for a fair value of $53.4 billion using $30.4 billion in term loans and cash on hand, and subsequently sold VMware's end-user computing business to KKR for $3.5 billion.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose significant debt financing activities and associated interest rate risk within Item 1. Intel explicitly quantifies the sensitivity of its interest expense to rate changes, stating that a 1% increase would increase annual interest expense by approximately $120 million due to fixed-rate debt swapped to floating-rate. Similarly, Broadcom discloses in Item 1 that it funded the cash portion of its VMware acquisition with $30.4 billion in term loans, directly linking its major capital resource action to debt issuance which creates the interest rate exposure described by Intel.

sentences.text: Taking into account fixed-rate debt that is swapped to floating-rate debt, a hypothetical increase in interest rates of 1% would result in an increase in annual interest expense of approximately $120 million from debt outstanding as of December 28, 2024 ($120 million from debt outstanding as of December 30, 2023).

We funded the cash portion of the VMware Merger consideration with net proceeds from the issuance of $30.4 billion in term loans under a credit agreement that we entered into on August 15, 2023, as well as cash on hand.
